standard_prerequisites.name: Noetherianity of the underlying topological space, and the reduced induced structure on a closed subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Properties of Spaces, labels spaces-properties-lemma-Noetherian-topology (invoked at proof line 2554) and spaces-properties-lemma-reduced-closed-subspace (invoked at proof line 2582)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first supplies the minimal element of the collection of counterexample supports; the second provides the ideal sheaf defining the reduced structure on that support.

core_obligations: Assume the collection of closed supports of counterexamples is nonempty, choose a minimal element $T$ using Noetherianity, and note $T \neq \emptyset$ because the zero sheaf admits the trivial filtration (proof lines 2539-2560).

Rule out a reducible $T = Z_1 \cup Z_2$: the splitting lemma writes $\mathcal{F}$ as an extension of sheaves supported on the strictly smaller closed pieces, each of which has the desired filtration by minimality, and combining the two filtrations contradicts the choice of $T$ (proof lines 2562-2577).

For irreducible $T$, use that a power of the ideal $\mathcal{J}$ of the reduced structure annihilates $\mathcal{F}$ to filter $\mathcal{F}$ by the submodules $\mathcal{J}^k\mathcal{F}$, whose successive subquotients are annihilated by $\mathcal{J}$, thereby reducing to the case $\mathcal{J}\mathcal{F} = 0$ (proof lines 2579-2594).

In the remaining case, identify $\mathcal{F}$ with a pushforward from the scheme theoretic support $T$ and apply the preparation lemma to obtain $0 \to i_*(\mathcal{I}^{\oplus r}) \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{Q} \to 0$ with $\mathcal{Q}$ supported in a proper closed subset; minimality gives the filtration for $\mathcal{Q}$, and the extension of the two filtrations is the required filtration for $\mathcal{F}$ (proof lines 2596-2612).
proof_roadmap: The irreducible case, and the final contradiction (proof lines 2596-2612).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a filtration of any coherent sheaf on a Noetherian algebraic space whose successive subquotients are pushforwards of ideal sheaves from reduced irreducible closed subspaces (statement lines 2520-2536). The proof runs the usual minimal counterexample argument on the support: a reducible support is split into two smaller pieces, the general irreducible case is reduced by filtering along the powers of the ideal of the support, and the remaining case is handled by a preparation lemma that exhibits the sheaf as an extension of a pushed forward ideal power and a sheaf supported in a proper closed subset. The minimal counterexample reduction and the final extension step are the substance, so the claim is H2.
